# Geometry and Surface Priors

Also called: Geometric constraints, Surface alignment, Depth priors

## Overview
This family of methods addresses the fundamental limitation of vanilla 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS): the production of "floating" volumetric ellipsoids that lack an explicit, watertight geometric boundary [9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment]. By aligning the discrete Gaussian representation with continuous geometric priors (such as SDFs, depth maps, or explicit meshes), these methods enforce positional and normal consistency to enable accurate mesh extraction, physically-based rendering, and robust initialization [9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment]. Unlike sibling methods that may rely solely on photometric loss or implicit constraints, this family explicitly integrates geometric supervision into the training or post-processing pipeline to ensure the Gaussians conform to physical surfaces [9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family share the goal of aligning the discrete Gaussian representation with a continuous geometric prior. The core mechanism involves adding geometric loss terms to the standard photometric rendering loss $\mathcal{L}_{rgb}$. These losses typically enforce two properties:
1.  **Positional Consistency:** Gaussian centers $\mathbf{c}_i$ are encouraged to lie on the zero-level set of a distance function (SDF or UDF) or align with metric depth estimates [9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment].
2.  **Normal Consistency:** The orientation of the Gaussians (derived from their covariance matrix or rotation quaternion) is aligned with the surface normal estimated from the geometric prior [9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment].

The total loss function generally takes the form:
$$ \mathcal{L}_{total} = \mathcal{L}_{rgb} + \lambda_{geo} \mathcal{L}_{geo} + \lambda_{norm} \mathcal{L}_{norm} $$
where $\mathcal{L}_{geo}$ is the geometric consistency loss and $\mathcal{L}_{norm}$ is the normal consistency loss [9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment]. The weights $\lambda_{geo}$ and $\lambda_{norm}$ are hyperparameters that balance photometric fidelity against geometric accuracy [9267-surface-and-geometry-alignment].

## Subtopics

### NeuSG
NeuSG [9172-neusg] integrates the NeuS [S1] implicit surface reconstruction framework into the 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) representation to transfer explicit surface properties to the discrete Gaussian primitives. It solves the problem of vanilla 3DGS producing "floating ellipsoids" rather than coherent surfaces by enforcing geometric consistency. Unlike siblings that use monocular depth or explicit mesh extraction, NeuSG directly couples a NeuS-style Signed Distance Function (SDF) with a Gaussian rasterizer [9172-neusg, S1, S2, unofficial].

### [Monocular Depth Scale Alignment](9183-monocular-depth-scale-alignment.md)
Monocular Depth Scale Alignment [9183-monocular-depth-scale-alignment] is a post-optimization step in 3D Gaussian Splatting pipelines that resolves the up-to-scale ambiguity inherent in multi-view reconstruction by aligning the metric scale of optimized 3D Gaussians with metric-scale monocular depth estimates [9183-monocular-depth-scale-alignment, S1, unofficial]. Unlike methods that integrate depth priors during training, this approach operates after the standard Gaussian optimization phase, fixing the Gaussian parameters and optimizing only a global scale factor [9183-monocular-depth-scale-alignment, S1, unofficial]. It is distinct from sibling methods like [NeuSG](9172-neusg.md) or [GSDF](9205-gsdf.md) which embed geometric losses into the training loop, and from [Sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting with Depth Priors](9185-sparse-view-3d-gaussian-splatting-with-depth-priors.md) which may rely on different initialization strategies.

### [Sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting with Depth Priors](9185-sparse-view-3d-gaussian-splatting-with-depth-priors.md)
This method [9185-sparse-view-3d-gaussian-splatting-with-depth-priors] addresses the challenge of 3D reconstruction from sparse-view inputs, where standard 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) suffers from geometric ambiguity and artifacts due to insufficient multi-view constraints. It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [NeuSG](9172-neusg.md) and [GSDF](9205-gsdf.md) by explicitly integrating depth priors estimated from pre-trained 2D monocular depth estimation networks to supervise the Gaussian distribution, rather than relying solely on implicit neural fields or surface extraction techniques [9185-sparse-view-3d-gaussian-splatting-with-depth-priors, S1].

### GSDF
GSDF [9205-gsdf] is a training optimization technique that aligns the discrete 3D Gaussian representation with a continuous Signed Distance Function (SDF) prior to enhance geometry reconstruction quality [9205-gsdf, S1]. It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [NeuSG](9172-neusg.md) by explicitly transferring surface properties from a neural SDF to the Gaussians, encouraging Gaussian centers to lie on the zero-level set and normals to align with the SDF gradient [9205-gsdf, S1].

### GaussianPro
#### definition
- [S1] A method that considers neighboring views' normal direction consistency to produce better reconstruction results.
#### step
- [S1] Introduces a progressive propagation strategy for updating Gaussians, considering normal consistency between neighboring views.
- [S1] Adds plane constraints to guide the growth of 3D Gaussian Splatting.

### 3DGSR
#### definition
- [S1] A method that encourages consistency between Signed Distance Function (SDF) and 3DGS to enhance geometry reconstruction quality.

### Gaussian Splatting Surface Refinement
#### definition
- [S2] Using pretrained volume rendering priors (UDF) to push Gaussians toward true surfaces by optimizing along the direction of increasing rendering weights, avoiding off-surface drift and discreteness.
- [S2] A post-training refinement strategy that uses a pretrained volume rendering prior to optimize Gaussian distributions toward true surfaces, particularly effective for open and thin structures.
#### step
- [S2] Integrate the prior into existing Gaussian Splatting variants (e.g., GaussianUDF, QGS) without modifying inference-time resource costs, as the prior network is bypassed during inference.
#### comparison
- [S2] Outperforms handcrafted renderers and closed-surface-tailored 3DGS methods on open and thin structures, where standard Gaussian distributions degrade severely.

## Background
The problem of "floating" Gaussians in standard 3DGS has been a primary driver for geometric priors. Early works like NeuSG [S1] adapted implicit surface representations (NeuS) to guide Gaussian placement. Subsequent works such as GSDF [S1] and 3DGSR [S1] formalized the consistency between SDFs and Gaussian attributes. More recent approaches leverage monocular depth estimators for scale alignment [9183-monocular-depth-scale-alignment, S1, unofficial] or sparse-view reconstruction [9185-sparse-view-3d-gaussian-splatting-with-depth-priors, S1]. Volume rendering priors, such as those in VRP-UDF [S2], have been used to refine surfaces, particularly for thin structures where standard methods fail [S2].
